Theme

Body, health & movement

hairstyle noun

also hairdo, hair style, do one’s hair, do someone’s hair, set someone’s hair, style hair

classical

Plaut. Am. 1.1.288: pēs, statūra, tōnsus, oculī (Lewis & Short: “the cut or mode of dressing the hair”)
Traupman 164, 167

tōnsus, tōnsūs m.

noun, fourth declension

the cut or style of the hair

(ante-classical (Lewis & Short))

Other words

  • cōmptus, cōmptūs m. — an ornament for the hair, a head-dress

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Lucr. 1.88 (Lewis & Short): an ornament for the hair or head, a head-dress; Traupman 161, 164

    A rare word, and in Lewis & Short an ornament for the hair rather than the style itself; Traupman uses it for a hairdo. To do someone’s hair is the verb cōmere; the cut or style of the hair is tōnsus.

  • cōmō, cōmere, cōmpsī, cōmptum — do (the hair), arrange, dress

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Pis. 25: capillōs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 160, 167

See also haircut, hairdresser, comb.
